clauses.reason: Terminated by express revocation. EO 9830, Part III, revokes the listed Executive orders including "No. 9052 of February 6, 1942." The enacting clause orders the whole of EO 9830 "it is hereby ordered as follows, effective May 1, 1947:" so the end is recorded as 1947-05-01. Part III has no separate date and the enacting clause orders Parts I, II and III alike 'effective May 1, 1947'; the alternative reading is that the revocation took effect on signing, 1947-02-24 (printed 12 FR 1259, 1947-02-25).

research_rationale:
Identity and text: read in full in the registered Federal Register original (7 FR 839-840, issue of 1942-02-10, PDF pages 3-4; grade original_representation_unverified, acceptable_as_original true). The order is headed 'Amending Subdivision VIII of Schedule A of the Civil Service Rules', signed February 6, 1942, bracket [No. 9052]. It amends Subdivision VIII of Schedule A by adding paragraph 30, 'The Solicitor of the Department of the Interior'. Inventory: the amending sentence (which runs across a page break) and item 30; the neighbouring orders on the same pages (EO 9051 and EO 9053) are not part of it. End: EO 9830, signed February 24, 1947, Part III reads "The following Executive orders are hereby revoked:" and lists "No. 9052 of February 6, 1942."; the held ACT record locates the provision in the official Federal Register text (12 FR 1259). EO 9830's own Rule II restates Schedule A (section 6.4(a)), and the held text of that restatement contains no entry for the Solicitor of the Department of the Interior.

savings.reason: EO 9830 as held contains no savings, exception or nothing-herein wording for the orders listed in Part III. Its restated Schedule A has no entry for the Solicitor of the Department of the Interior (the word 'Solicitor' appears there only for other offices). Whether individuals appointed under paragraph 30 before 1947-05-01 kept their status is not shown by any held source and is not claimed.
